title: fix(plugin-audit): sys_activity.actor_avatar_url carries the acting user's profile image, from the actor_name memo read
body:
Fixes #22527
Clause-②: no

## What this changes

`sys_activity` declares `actor_avatar_url` (`sys-activity.object.ts`, beside `actor_id` and `actor_name`). Its one writer, `plugin-audit`'s `writeAudit` (`audit-writers.ts`), never filled it. So every activity row carried a null avatar, even for a user with a profile image, and the record History tab and the record activity feed showed the generic avatar for everyone.

The writer now fills `actor_avatar_url` from the acting user's `sys_user.image`, through the per-user memo that already fills `actor_name` (landed in `d1d42ec57`). There is no second lookup path. The memo becomes `resolveActorSnapshot`, which makes ONE `sys_user` read, projects the title column and `image`, and returns `{ name, avatarUrl }`.

- **Name:** unchanged. The title column comes from `titleFieldOf`, with the same masking and `internal` skips. The text rule is now one shared helper, `titleTextOf`, which `resolveLookupTitles` uses too, byte-identical to the inline rule it replaces.
- **Avatar:** the stored value, copied verbatim. It is not rewritten (see the measurement below).
- **No image** stays null. **No user** (a system write) stays null, and no `sys_user` read happens (ADR-0118 D1; how the system actor is shown is the renderer's choice).
- `image` is projected only when `sys_user` declares that column. A projection therefore never names a column the object lacks, which would also cost the name.

ADR-0049 applies: a declared column gets its writer. `sys-activity.object.ts` is untouched, and so are objectui and `content/docs/releases/`.

## Measurement: the column, and what the renderers expect

- **Column.** `sys_user.image` (`packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-user.object.ts`, `image: Field.url`). ADR-0092 Tier 1 says "`image` — avatar URL." It is a `url` field, not an `image`-type field, so ADR-0104's file-reference shape (a `sys_file` id) does not apply to it.
- **Producers.** objectui's profile page at the pinned `.objectui-sha` `20c6d351` (`apps/console/src/pages/system/ProfilePage.tsx:115`) uploads the file and then calls `updateUser({ image: result.url })`. That is `POST /api/v1/auth/update-user`, which the card measured. `record-validator.ts` records the shape it stores: `/api/v1/storage/files/FILE_ID`. Its `URL_RE` validates the column on write.
- **Renderers at `20c6d351`:**
  - `packages/plugin-detail/src/renderers/record-history.tsx:201` maps `user_avatar: r.actor_avatar_url ?? null`. `HistoryTimeline.tsx:217-221` passes it as the `src` of `AvatarImage`.
  - `packages/plugin-detail/src/renderers/recordActivityFeed.ts:807` maps `actorAvatarUrl: row.actor_avatar_url ?? undefined`. `RecordActivityTimeline.tsx:553-555` passes it as the `src` of an img element.
- **Verdict.** Both renderers want a URL that goes straight into an image source, and the column stores exactly that. The profile page renders the same `user.image` the same way. This is not a fork, and no transform is applied.
- **Bound.** Both columns are `Field.url` with no `maxLength`, so they share one declared bound. A value that fits the source fits the copy.

## Pins (`packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/activity-actor-name.test.ts`, on the real `ObjectQL` engine)

The new describe block is `[#22527] sys_activity.actor_avatar_url`. It uses the file's existing counting driver double; no new double is added.

1. **Pin:** a user with `sys_user.image` set writes that exact value on the activity row, on create, update and delete alike. `actor_id` and `actor_name` name the same user.
2. **Control:** a user with no image leaves `actor_avatar_url` null. The name still lands from the same read.
3. **Control:** a system write leaves it null and reads `sys_user` zero times.
4. **Memo:** a predicate update over 3 rows makes exactly ONE `sys_user` read. That read's projection carries both `name` and `image`, and all 3 rows carry both values. A later write by the same user inside the window makes no read.

The fixture now declares `sys_activity.actor_avatar_url` and `sys_user.image`, as the shipped objects do. The six `#22510` pins are unchanged and still green.

## Ablations (committed state; writer blob `7e8ede39cac1`, the same at the final head)

Both ablations went through `node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` in wrap mode, inside a script that also carries a restore trap. Each restore was proven by the tool and again by hand: the blob equals HEAD's and `git diff HEAD` is empty. The subject resolves by a relative import into `src/`, so no `dist/` leg applies.

- **Drop the stamp.** The anchor `...(actor.avatarUrl ? { actor_avatar_url: actor.avatarUrl } : {}),` was deleted: anchor 1 → 0, blob `7e8ede39cac1` → `77824c05976f`. The result was `Tests 2 failed | 8 passed (10)`. Pins 1 and 4 went red with `expected undefined to be '/api/v1/storage/files/file_grace_avat…'`; both controls and every name pin stayed green. That is the expected direction. After restore the blob is back to `7e8ede39cac1`.
- **Bypass the memo.** `const hit = actorSnapshotCache.get(userId);` was replaced with `const hit = undefined as any;`: blob → `1ced12124c1a`. The result was `Tests 2 failed | 8 passed (10)`. The `#22510` read-count pin and the new memo pin 4 both went red with `expected 3 to be 1`. After restore the blob is back to `7e8ede39cac1`.

## Local verification (final head `980e354e40`, after merging `origin/main` at `5fb1746611`)

- **Typecheck.** `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-audit typecheck` exited 0, and `check:test-typecheck` reported OK (the new test file compiles under `tsconfig.test.json`).
- **Tests.** `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-audit test` gave `Test Files 45 passed (45)` and `Tests 714 passed (714)`.
- **Gates.** `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derived 67 commands from this diff, and all 67 were run with their exits recorded. `--ran` reports: `67 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 65 run, 2 NOT-MEASURED`.
  - The two exit-3 prerequisite refusals were `check:i18n` and `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`.
  - `check:i18n` was re-run after its prerequisite closure was built and passed: `OK (9 package(s) — all bundles in sync, no undeclared authoring keys)`.
  - `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` was re-run after a full workspace build (`turbo run build`, 71 of 72 tasks from cache) and passed: `107 published require entry point(s) across 66 package(s) load`.
- **ESLint, targeted.** `eslint --no-inline-config --format json` was run on the 2 changed TypeScript files and reported `files=2 errors=0 warnings=0`. The population comes from `eslint.config.mjs`: the `**/*.{ts,tsx,mts,cts,js,jsx,mjs,cjs}` and `packages/**/*.{ts,tsx,mts,cts}` objects. This narrowing cannot change a verdict on any untouched file, because the config never enables type-aware linting (no `parserOptions.project`, no `projectService`). The repo-wide `pnpm lint` belongs to CI.
- **Changeset.** `.changeset/22527-activity-actor-avatar.md` is a `patch` for `@objectstack/plugin-audit`.

## Acceptance notes

- **Snapshot semantics.** These match the name's. Rows written before this change keep a null avatar; nothing backfills them. A new image shows on rows written after the 30-second memo window.
- **A malformed stored image could cost an activity row.** The engine validates the copied value against `actor_avatar_url`'s `Field.url` shape on insert. A `sys_user.image` value that bypassed the identical validation on its own write (a raw SQL edit, for example) would make that row's activity insert refuse. The existing durability path would report that at `error`. I have not measured any producer of such a value: the console uploader, better-auth `update-user` and OAuth sign-up all store validated URLs. Noted only.
- **Observation, not measured.** The sibling column `sys_comment.author_avatar_url` is client-written. At `20c6d351`, `packages/app-shell/src/views/RecordDetailView.tsx:2085` and `:2124` write `author_avatar_url: 'avatar' in currentUser ? (currentUser as any).avatar : undefined`. objectui's own profile page reads the signed-in user's avatar as `user.image` (`ProfilePage.tsx:153`), not `avatar`, so this may always write undefined. That reading is unverified (no reach measured), it lives in objectui, and it is outside this card. There is no carrier.
